findings: All 24 final wrapped-off/threaded image cases match the unhooked oracle exactly, with matching checked backend state. Fresh poses and changed materials visibly alter both lit output and shadow maps.

The four final runs retain 84 alternating paired samples. Lit completion savings are 0.0339 and -0.9983 ms; shadow savings are 0.3208 and 0.5722 ms per modeled normal/extra pair. Across-run workload times drift substantially; no significant full-scene gain is established.

The separate probe observes one drain for GetVertexShader after queued effect work, and one for GetVertexShaderConstantF after a new CommitChanges, in every lit/shadow round. A getter following the first drain reports zero; it is not proof that it never synchronizes.

Production instancing queries the bound shader when capturing a group and saves constant registers before submitting batches. These measured boundaries justify investigating their interaction with worker submission; drain counts alone do not establish elapsed blocking cost.
limits: 256x256 synthetic geometry/material workload: 288 groups of 25 meshes, six bones. No native material-source computation, terrain, water reflections, Present or full scene.
Both timed modes use the same optimistic bulk-after-second prototype; this is not the full installed beta.13 native group path. Wrapped-off mode still incurs external passthrough hooks.
Each sample averages four separately fenced regular/extra pairs. Fresh poses change between pair members. Separate lit/shadow timings must not be added or converted to gameplay FPS.
Backend state checks cover all vertex/pixel float constant registers, twelve render states, 104 sampler values and two stream frequencies, not all resource lifetime/failure behavior.

The diagnostic identifies drain counters, not their elapsed cost or the attribution of all drains in the benchmark. It reads counters without adding queue commands or drains; earlier getters can mask subsequent synchronization.

Preliminary 84 pairs are retained separately; final runs follow the main-name embedding macro addition needed by the barrier diagnostic. The draw workload logic did not change. Preliminary binaries were subsequently replaced in TEMP; their captured hashes are retained, not reverified from current binaries.
No external installation, runtime plugin change, game/WorldBuilder launch, multiplayer proof or FPS success.
